script: [serious] November 24th, 1971. The day before Thanksgiving. A quiet man in a dark suit buys a one-way ticket from Portland to Seattle, under the name Dan Cooper. He orders a drink... then hands the flight attendant a note. [whispers] He has a bomb in his briefcase. His demands: two hundred thousand dollars in twenty-dollar bills, and four parachutes. In Seattle, he gets both, and lets every passenger go. Then the plane takes off again. Somewhere over southwest Washington, at night, in the rain, he lowers the rear stairs... and jumps. He was never seen again. Nine years later, an eight-year-old boy by the Columbia River dug up five thousand eight hundred dollars of the ransom, still in rubber bands. Over a thousand suspects. Forty-five years. In 2016, the FBI stopped actively investigating. It's still the only unsolved hijacking of its kind in American aviation history. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number four. Which file should we open next?
